chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it makes the national podium broad enough to see beyond the champion story. The Best in Japan third-place card is not just rank text; it is a finalist photograph, a tournament logo, a finals route, and a preserved coordinate in the 2002 apparatus.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan third place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.3 Trainer at source index 255.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.3 Trainer Battle Road Summer print was awarded to third-place winners of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan deciding tournament.
Bulbapedia's Elite Four Trainer page places the Battle Road Summer 2002 finals in Tokyo on August 17, after regional events between July 20 and August 11.

Bulbapedia's photography article says the top four ranking players of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan tournament had their photographs featured on Trainer cards with the event logo superimposed on the image.
TCGCollector's No.3 Trainer entries preserve the Best in Japan Deciding Match third-place recognition text for Junior and Senior tournament versions, supporting the rank-specific finals lane.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series introduced the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says Battle Road Summer 2002, unlike Spring, culminated in a Best in Japan final with a new card awarded to top ranking players.

Pokumon says Junior league winners of Battle Road Summer 2002 were invited to the International Tropical Mega Battle 2002 in Hawaii, giving the Summer apparatus an international edge beyond the regional and national trophies.

No named illustrator or designer is promoted for this exact row from the attached sources; the visual-credit note is therefore kept as winner photograph / unpromoted production design rather than an artist attribution.

As judged collector texture, this No.3 Trainer matters because it turns national third place into a personal image-object: the route, rank, logo, and finalist photograph all have to line up before an agent treats a listing as the Best in Japan third-place card.

Agents should preserve No.3 rank, Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan finals route, source index 255, August 17 Tokyo finals context, winner-photograph construction, Battle Road Summer 2002 logo, and non-equivalence with regional No.3 Trainer, Best in Japan No.1/No.2, Elite Four Trainer, Worlds, Neo Road, or generic No.3 Trainer listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan No.3 Trainer: third place with a face
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the card that keeps the national podium from narrowing into a single heroic point. Third place is still a person, still a finals route, still a photograph inside an official card. That is the kind of assembly this catalog is trying to preserve: not only who won, but how far the memory apparatus reached before it stopped.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller story, slab label, or agent memory says No.3 Trainer, Ｎｏ.３トレーナー, Battle Road Summer 2002, Best in Japan, finals, Tokyo, August 17 2002, winner photograph, competition logo, regional No.3 Trainer, No.1 Trainer, No.2 Trainer, Elite Four Trainer, World Championships, Neo Road, Tropical Mega Battle, or Secret Super Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this row by No.3 Trainer rank plus Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan finals route and winner-photograph card construction, not by famous trophy wording alone.
steps: Confirm the rank is No.3 Trainer / third place, not No.1, No.2, or Elite Four Trainer.
Confirm the route is Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan third place prize, source index 255, not a regional third-place prize.
Look for the finals context: Tokyo final on August 17, 2002 after the July-August regional circuit.
Check whether the card construction includes a winner photograph with the Battle Road Summer 2002 competition logo superimposed; this is a core identity clue, not merely decoration.

Separate this row from Battle Road Summer 2002 regional No.3 Trainer, Spring 2002 regional trophies, Best in Japan No.1/No.2, Elite Four Trainer top-four prize, Worlds No.3 Trainer, Neo Road trophy cards, Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, and Kamex Mega Battle.
Do not promote a named illustrator unless a stronger row-level source appears; record the art lane as winner photograph / unpromoted production design.
If a seller offers winner identity, photograph, certificate, tournament paperwork, slab label, or provenance story, treat it as evidence to inspect and hash, not automatic authenticity.

Before any trade gate or spendability decision, require seller-controlled front/back images plus close-ups of title/rank, event text, photograph/logo area, surface/corners, and slab/cert/provenance evidence if claimed.
